name: p2c-burst-pilot-aime-v1
supersedes: The P2B 240 s sustained-rate calibration is closed as a documented stop. This is a new pre-declaration for the next cycle, not a retry or a threshold change; every P2B record remains authoritative for that cycle.
basis: P2B-CALIBRATION-STOP.md: no rate is in the 15-40% band at 240 s. The queue is stable at <=1000/h and above capacity at >=1025/h; the 25/h grid cannot resolve the knee because realised-rate sampling error and batch-size-dependent service time are both larger than the step.

The AIME 2025+2026 preview carries a reproducible 4k->8k quality slope: +18.8 points on 96 responses (p=5.3e-4), and +17.2 points on 87 historical AIME pairs. This is the fact that works; it is used here as the positive control and quality endpoint.

The measured service-time mix is about 80 s at 4k and 150 s at 8k for signal requests, and about 24 s for 1k filler. A 32-slot rig therefore clears a fixed4k burst but not a fixed8k burst of the same shape, which is exactly the mechanism contrast to test.

P2B-CALIBRATION-STOP.md section 6: a next cycle should control the warm-up backlog. A scripted burst does that directly: the baseline is below capacity, the burst is deterministic, and the recovery window is part of the same trace.

pool.name: aime-2025-2026-v1
pool.question_set: all 60 items: 48 measured in the preview plus 12 reserve items

design.purpose: Test whether the pressure-cut policy preserves AIME quality and improves correct-on-time goodput under a controlled burst, without using the fragile sustained-rate calibration that stopped P2B.
design.trace_shape_note: 600/h baseline for 420 s, 64 requests at 4/s for 16 s, then 600/h recovery. At 600/h the rig is below capacity, so there is no warm-up backlog cliff; the burst is the only pressure source.
design.why_64: A 32-slot, 150 s fixed8k burst leaves the second wave waiting about 150 s and finishing about 300 s after arrival, while fixed4k finishes the same burst in about 165 s. The burst is large enough to separate the arms and small enough that a working cut can still save the second wave.

endpoints.primary: correct_on_time signal responses, pooled over both traces (240 responses per arm)
secondary: cap rate, missing-box rate, thinking tokens
queue time, service time, p50/p90 latency
cuts, cut-after-close, pressure fraction, admission budget split
endpoints.failed_outcomes: Caps, missing outputs, late answers and errors stay in the planned denominator. Correct-on-time requires a normal completion, a correct answer, and client receipt <= deadline.

validity_requires: all planned phases present and injection_valid
live phases have at least one in-flight cut and positive pressure at waiting >= 8
no cut after the close token
live phases show both a 4096 and an 8192 admission
fixed4k and fixed8k phases have zero cuts
stop_if: fixed8k - fixed4k eventual accuracy is below 8 points (the known slope did not reproduce)
live correct-on-time is not above fixed4k
live eventual accuracy is below fixed4k
live eventual accuracy is more than 15 points below fixed8k
decision.inconclusive: Valid and slope reproduced, but the live effect is between the stop and go thresholds. Record it; do not spend the confirmatory GPU block without a new pre-declaration.

power.note: Stage A has 120 responses/arm (2 seeds, one trace); Stage B adds an independent trace for 240/arm. At ICC 0.2-0.6 and 20% discordance the 80% MDE is roughly 10-14 points. This is a screening pilot, not a powered P2: a null result is not proof of no effect, and a positive result is a reason to run a confirmatory block.
